notes_for_editor: Princess Sophia death toll: NRHP gives 353, Lighthouse Friends 343 (story states both). Dates for the Princess May come from 1910 newspapers (Seattle Star: 2 a.m. grounding, said to have sunk; Salt Lake Tribune: total loss, passengers at the lighthouse); the 3 September refloating is from Lighthouse Friends only. The Light-House Board 1901 report page was not determinable from OCR. Putnam page number uncertain (scan 198). Annual reports 1902-1917 are not in the corpus, so the early keepers' work and fog-signal hours are not documented here; 1918 Commissioner hits were ambiguous and not used. Roster is USLHS only; 1960s Coast Guard crew are in the roster table but not named in prose. Record's characteristic 'Fl W 10s' and 15.5 m tower height not verified by a source read here. NRHP gives the 1935 lantern's light as flashing white, 17 mile range, but also fixed white originally; the Bulletin shows group flashing by 1918. Record says tower 'built 1935': correct for present building.
